title: Stabilize CUDA Graph capture/replay for multi-stream decode
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Our multi-stream decode path (prefill on stream A, decode on stream B) gives large latency/throughput wins by overlapping prefill and autoregressive decode. However, switching to CUDA Graph capture/replay to eliminate launch overhead exposes nondeterministic capture failures and replay misbehavior in two categories: (1) capture instability when workspace pointers or allocator state change between captures, and (2) replay correctness issues when underlying library heuristics (cuBLAS/cuDNN) pick different kernels between capture and replay. Goal: make CUDA Graphs production-safe for multi-stream decode across common sequence-length distributions and batch sizes while preserving overlap benefits.
acceptance_criteria: CUDA Graph capture succeeds deterministically for standard prefill+decode scenarios used in internal benchmarks (seq_len 8..1024, batch 1..8) on NVIDIA A100 and H100 in 95% of runs
Replay produces bit-identical logits/kv cache updates for a representative evaluation prompt set compared to baseline non-graph path within numeric tolerance (float16 eps), validated by automated CI
End-to-end latency and throughput on our decode microbench improves or remains equal to prior non-graph multi-stream path for production configs; no regression >5% in p95 latency
Graceful fallback: when capture or replay fails, runtime falls back to the non-graph multi-stream codepath and emits structured telemetry for root-cause analysis
tasks: Audit current allocator and workspace lifetimes used during capture; identify sources of pointer instability
Introduce a deterministic stream pool abstraction with stable stream IDs and pinned CUDA stream assignment for capture/replay
Force deterministic algorithm selection for cuBLAS/cuDNN where possible and document flags/configs required
Preallocate and pin all staging buffers used during capture to a capture-specific arena to ensure pointer stability
Implement a capture validation mode in CI that runs repeated captures/replays across permutations of batch/seq length and checks for replay drift
Add telemetry events for capture start/end/failure reasons and replay checksum deltas
Performance test and compare against baseline across A100/H100 for a matrix of batch x seq_len workloads

decisions: Use a dedicated capture arena with deterministic allocation ordering to stabilize device pointers during CUDA Graph capture

Adopt a small set of deterministic flags for vendor libraries (e.g., set CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING as needed in CI) instead of attempting to control heuristics at the kernel scheduler level
Keep multi-stream prefill/decode split but require fixed stream IDs during a capture session; do not capture across contexts where stream assignments may change
Implement a conservative checksum-based replay validation that runs in CI and can be enabled in staging clusters to detect silent drift early
risks: Library-level nondeterminism (cuBLAS/cuDNN) may not be fully controllable on some driver versions leading to platform-dependent flakiness
Preallocation to stabilize pointers increases peak memory usage and could reduce max batch for some Dedicated SKUs
Telemetry and fallback paths add control-plane complexity; incomplete instrumentation may make failures hard to triage
Edge cases: mixed-precision kernels and fused attention kernels may diverge numerically; need to define acceptable tolerances
next_steps: Expand CI capture-validation matrix to cover seq_len {8,32,128,512,1024} x batch {1,2,4,8} on A100/H100
Merge fallback wiring so runtime emits telemetry and falls back immediately on capture or replay failure
Coordinate with infra to run expanded perf jobs on Dedicated nodes to measure memory impact and throughput changes
Draft Console feature brief for CUDA Graph opt-in toggle for Dedicated customers and include known limitations
